# NoteSync Markdown Profile

<!-- generated by `python3 -m notesync profile` from notesync/capabilities.py; do not edit by hand -->

NoteSync keeps one markdown file per note in sync with Apple Notes and Evernote. Each note app gets the file rendered into its own rich text, and edits made there are flattened back into markdown. That round trip is exact only for the subset below: write within it and the note looks right everywhere and never drifts.

## Rules

1. **One line is one paragraph.** Line breaks are kept exactly as typed, so do
   not hard-wrap prose; a trailing double space or `\` means nothing.
2. **Blank lines are kept as typed.** Use them the way the note should look.
3. **The file name is the title.** Do not repeat it as a leading `# ` heading
   (every endpoint already shows the title), and do not add YAML front matter
   -- NoteSync manages its own `ns:` header, anything else becomes note text.
4. **Use only the constructs below.** Anything else is not lost, but shows as
   literal markdown in the note apps.
5. **Code, diagrams and commands go in fenced code blocks with a language**
   (`text` for plain text). Inside a fence nothing is interpreted and every
   space is kept. Prefer ```` ```mermaid ```` over drawing ASCII diagrams.
6. **Run the linter when you are done:** `python3 -m notesync lint <file>`
   (from the NoteSync checkout). `--fix` rewrites lenient spellings into the
   canonical ones; it never changes meaning.

## Constructs

| Construct | Write it as | Evernote | Apple Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Headings 1-3 | `# `, `## `, `### ` + text | rendered | rendered |
| Headings 4-6 | `#### ` ... | literal text | literal text |
| Bold / italic | `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `***both***` | rendered | rendered |
| Inline code | `` `code` `` | rendered | rendered |
| Links | `[text](https://url)` | rendered | literal text |
| Bullet lists | `- item` | rendered | rendered |
| Ordered lists | `1. item`, numbered 1..n without gaps | rendered | rendered |
| Nested lists | indent by the parent marker width: 2 spaces under `- `, 3 under `1. ` | rendered | rendered |
| Checklists | `- [ ] todo` / `- [x] done` | literal text | literal text |
| Code blocks | ```` ```lang ```` ... ```` ``` ```` | rendered | rendered |
| Block quotes | `> text`, `>` for a blank quote line | rendered | literal text |
| Horizontal rule | `---` on its own line | rendered | literal text |
| Tables | `\| a \| b \|` then `\|---\|---\|`, one row per line | rendered | rendered |
| Indentation and space runs | kept as typed | rendered | rendered |
| Math | `$...$` inline, `$$` block lines | literal text | literal text |
| Images / attachments | `![alt](path)` | literal text | literal text |
| Raw HTML | - | literal text | literal text |
| Strikethrough / footnotes / highlights | - | literal text | literal text |

## Details

(`⏎` in an example marks a line break.)

- **Headings 1-3.** Heading text is literal: endpoints bold whole headings, so `**` inside a heading is dropped. Apple stores h1/h2 as 24/18px bold and h3 as a bold underlined line. Do not put `**` inside headings.
  - accepted: `#  Spaced` -> canonical `# Spaced`
  - accepted: `## **Bold** head` -> canonical `## Bold head`
- **Headings 4-6.** Use `###` or a bold line instead.
- **Bold / italic.** Emphasis does not nest (no italic inside bold). Apple drops italic from CJK text, so italic spans containing CJK stay literal there. Use `*`, not `_`, for emphasis.
- **Inline code.** Apple has no inline code style: it becomes a Courier run. On Apple, inline code stays literal when it contains CJK (Courier has no CJK glyphs) and when a line is nothing but inline code (Apple would turn it into a monospaced paragraph). Keep other words on a line that holds inline code.
- **Links.** Apple strips href on write, so links stay literal there. Use absolute http(s) URLs.
- **Bullet lists.** `+` is not a bullet here (TeX lines start with `+`). Use `-` for bullets.
  - accepted: `* star ⏎ * two` -> canonical `- star ⏎ - two`
- **Ordered lists.** Numbers must run 1, 2, 3 ... inside a list. Evernote also renders a list that resumes after a paragraph (`start`); Apple cannot store a start number, so a list that is split by paragraphs or blank lines stays literal there. Keep ordered lists tight (no blank lines between items).
  - accepted: `1.  wide ⏎ 2.   gap` -> canonical `1. wide ⏎ 2. gap`
- **Nested lists.** Indent children exactly under the parent's text.
  - accepted: `- a ⏎     - four` -> canonical `- a ⏎   - four`
- **Code blocks.** Content is verbatim: no markdown inside, whitespace kept. The fence lines stay visible inside the block (they carry the language tag and delimit the block for round trips). Evernote: code block box; Apple: monospaced paragraphs. Always close fences and give a language (`text` for plain text). Draw diagrams with ```` ```mermaid ````, not ASCII art.
- **Block quotes.** Apple drops `<blockquote>` on write, so quotes stay literal there.
  - accepted: `>tight` -> canonical `> tight`
- **Horizontal rule.** Apple accepts `<hr>` but turns it into blank lines once the note settles, so rules stay literal there. Leave a blank line above `---` (right under text, standard markdown reads it as a heading underline).
  - accepted: `***` -> canonical `---`
  - accepted: `___` -> canonical `---`
- **Tables.** Column alignment is not kept (canonical separator is `|---|`). Apple stores tables as native table objects. Every row needs the same number of cells.
  - accepted: `| a | b | ⏎ | :--- | ---: | ⏎ | 1 | 2 |` -> canonical `| a | b | ⏎ |---|---| ⏎ | 1 | 2 |`
  - accepted: `|a|b| ⏎ |-|-|` -> canonical `| a | b | ⏎ |---|---|`
- **Indentation and space runs.** Written as non-breaking spaces so neither endpoint collapses them. Tabs are not preserved outside code blocks; trailing whitespace is always dropped. Indent with spaces, not tabs.
- **Math.** Shown as TeX source; nothing inside is parsed as markdown. Rendering as images is planned, not implemented.
- **Images / attachments.** The md reference stays literal. A note that holds an image or attachment inside the endpoint is frozen (never synced).
- **Raw HTML.** Use markdown syntax; raw HTML is shown as text.

## Example

````markdown
Short intro paragraph, one line per paragraph.

## Setup

1. Install the tool
2. Run `make build`
   - on macOS use `brew`

| Option | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-v` | verbose |

```bash
# comments stay comments
make build   # spacing is kept
```

> Quotes render in Evernote and stay literal in Apple Notes.
````
